plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY10 planning spoken persuasive texts for a purpose and audience; VC2E5LA03 language that suits audience and purpose; VC2E5LY01 presenting an opinion
plan.shape: model, guide, apply: the teacher plans the week's model speech (more shade trees) aloud, students practise matching audiences and think-feel-do, then plan their own speech
plan.criticalFeature: an audience you can picture tells you what to say: name who, then what they should think, feel and do
decisionPoints: the choice check: the clearest position
the exit board: audience and think-feel-do for a new speech
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. This week: write my own speech, for the ear.
plan.catchUp: Students who missed Weeks 6-7 use the Toolkit page and the planner frame.

slides.notes: Open the speech-writing week. One line: this week every one of you writes your own speech.

slides.title: For the teacher: Week 8 at a glance
lines: Students write a 2-minute speech (about 250-300 words) across five sessions.
Your model all week: Our school needs more shade trees. Write it live; don't pre-write it.
Each session's Worksheet ends with that part of their speech. Keep the sheets together in a folder.
Speech Day is Week 9 Session 2: confirm the audience this week.
slides.notes: Teacher-facing only. Plan: S1 issue and audience, S2 evidence and order, S3 opening, S4 middle and a story, S5 conclusion, timing and cue cards.

Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Students need their Toolkit and Week 5 published piece. A folder per student for the week's sheets.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to plan a speech for a purpose and an audience.
successCriteria: I can pick an issue and a clear position.
I can name my audience and what they should think, feel and do.
I can predict the toughest listener and plan an answer.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week you write your own speech. It starts with who you're talking to.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: What fires you up?
lines: Something at school, at home or in the world that should change.
If you had two minutes and a microphone, what would you say?

notes.answer: open - any issue the student cares about
beats: SAY: Two minutes. A microphone. Everyone listening.
What would you change?
ASK: School, home or the world: where is your issue?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, 1, 2 or 3... show me.
EXPECT: a mix of 1, 2 and 3
ASK: Tell your partner your issue in one sentence.
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: We should... or ... has to stop.
SAY: Your Week 5 issue is welcome. So is a brand new one.
trap: picking an issue nobody can act on.
Fix: ask who could actually change this?
notes.prep: Low-entry launch: every student names an issue. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: The side you take on an issue.
slides.example: My position: our school needs more shade trees.

notes.answer: the side you take on an issue
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Position. Say it with me. Position.
SAY: The side you take on an issue.
SAY: My position: our school needs more shade trees.
ASK: What is the difference between an issue and a position?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: the issue is the topic; the position is my side
trap: giving a topic as a position, like trees.
Fix: ask what about trees? Student adds should or must.
notes.prep: Position is the claim of a speech.

rows: Too little shade in our yard
Our school needs more shade trees.
Kids need shade to play safely.

notes.answer: issue, position, audience, think, feel, do
beats: POINT to Audience.
SAY: I picked the people who can actually plant trees.
Not the Preps. They can't buy trees.
POINT to Think and Feel.
SAY: One idea to stick, one feeling to stir.
Worried first, then hopeful, so they want to act.
POINT to Do.
SAY: A small, exact action. Ten trees. Before summer.
ASK: Which row tells me what to say in my speech?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: audience
trap: Fix: say if you can't picture their faces, the audience is too big.
notes.stretch: Predict what the business manager will say.
notes.help: Use the frame: I think, I'm talking to, I want them to.
notes.prep: The week's model speech. Think aloud; students copy nothing yet. Critical feature: picture the audience.

slides.title: Who's listening?
slides.pivot: ask who can actually make it happen?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: why that audience?

items.text: Longer lunch. 1 the principal, 2 the Preps, 3 the bus driver
Turn off screens at dinner. 1 the council, 2 families, 3 the canteen
A new skate park. 1 the library, 2 the Preps, 3 the local council
Stop littering at recess. 1 students, 2 the mayor, 3 farmers
Protect polar bear habitat. 1 a toy shop, 2 world leaders, 3 the Preps

say: Pick the audience that can make it happen.
trap: picking the audience that would like the idea most.
Fix: ask who has the power to say yes?
notes.stretch: Name a second audience who could help.
notes.help: Ask: who is in charge of this?

options.text: Trees are kind of nice, I guess.
Our school needs ten new shade trees by summer.
Here are some facts about trees.

notes.answer: B - sure, specific and takes a side
beats: SAY: Three speakers start their speech.
ASK: Which position is clearest?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: what makes B sure?
Less -> ask which one takes a side, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. A side, a number, a deadline.
trap: pointing to C because facts sound strong.
Fix: ask what does C want us to do?
notes.prep: Decision point before students plan. Under 80% means one more wobbly-to-clear rewrite together.

slides.title: Think, feel, do
slides.pivot: write the Do first, then the feeling that gets them there
slides.followUp: cold call one board: why that feeling?

items.text: Speech: walk to school on Wednesdays. Audience: families.
items.answer: Think: walking is easy. Feel: excited. Do: walk on Wednesdays.

items.text: Speech: no plastic straws. Audience: the canteen.
items.answer: Think: straws hurt sea life. Feel: guilty. Do: stop selling them.

items.text: Speech: more books in the library. Audience: the principal.
items.answer: Think: reading matters. Feel: proud. Do: buy fifty books.

say: Three words or short phrases on your board: think, feel, do.
trap: a Do that is too big, like save the planet.
Fix: student shrinks it to one action this week.
notes.help: Start with Do. What should they actually do?

slides.title: Plan my speech
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by planning your own speech: issue, position, audience, think, feel, do.
slides.frame: I think ___. I'm talking to ___. I want them to ___.

notes.answer: a plan with an issue, a clear position, an audience and think-feel-do
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Your plan for your own speech. The last section is the one that matters most.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: can you picture their faces? What should they do?
ASK: Tell your partner your position and your Do.
30 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: a clear side and one action
trap: Fix: student names one group who could say yes.
notes.stretch: Extension: one speech for two audiences, then the toughest listener.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a plan started, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent planning of their own speech; S2 builds on it. SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in the student's own speech plan

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A speech asks for a water bottle refill station at the park.
Name the best audience, and what they should think, feel and do.

notes.answer: e.g. the council; plastic waste is a problem; hopeful; build one by summer
beats: SAY: A new speech. Plan the audience and think, feel, do.
ASK: Write the audience and think, feel, do.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: the council or the park's owners; one action
RECORD who names everyone as the audience. Conference list for S2.
trap: an audience with no power, like park visitors only.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new speech. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: What is one thing your audience should feel by the end of your speech?

notes.answer: open - worried, hopeful, proud, fired up
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you about your position and your audience?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: What is one thing your audience
should feel by the end of your speech?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: worried, hopeful, proud, fired up
notes.prep: Plans go in the speech folder for S2. SC2.
